claim.text: A standalone Rust executable can parse and solve a finite Horn-clause Prolog subset without executing or loading the historical C GNU Prolog engine or compatibility FFI
claim.scope: Rust-only CLI, Horn facts/rules, lists, variables, finite-term unification, DFS search and bounded resources; ELF64 and i686 ELF32 Linux
assumptions: Rust standard-library implementation, no imported runtime code from GNU Prolog C
Occurs-check and float bitwise identity are intentional temporary semantic differences
forbidden_promotions: No complete GNU Prolog rewrite claim
No ISO Prolog or rational-tree equivalence claim
No WAM or finite-domain solver claim
No correctness proof for all programs
No broad performance or memory-safety proof

specification.intended_object: Single Rust-native parser, AST, unifier, clause-instantiation engine, choice stack and CLI entrypoint
invariants: No C bridge dynamic link at runtime
Clause order and depth-first answer order retained in supported subset
Fresh clause variable identities on every invocation
Malformed input and resource budgets yield bounded errors
Source parser rejects nested terms beyond limit and nonfinite floats
known_answer_cases: f(X,X) matches f(a,a) but not f(a,b)
Recursive loop with low step limit errors

implementation.commit: native rewrite branch at preregistration, CI result records subsequent exact head
implementation.environment: Rust 1.85.1 standard library, Ubuntu 24.04 native Linux ELF64 and i686 ELF32
implementation.live_entrypoint: cargo run from repository root invoking gprolog-rs <source.pl> <query>
implementation.representation: Rust enum Term, clause/query variable IDs, cloned substitutions, explicit depth-first choice stack; no WAM yet

metric.name: Correct CLI answers, parser/engine unit tests, metamorphic tests and absence of C engine dependency
metric.units: tests and execution paths per ABI
equivalence_attacks: Deep parser nesting and seeded malformed token corpus

black_box: Native Rust CLI output for ancestor/append/member/failure and errors
structural: ELF header checked on both ABIs
Dynamic library check excludes libgprolog and earlier float-decimal C ABI dependencies
Root Cargo workspace only includes native Rust package
property_based: Seeded 512-case deterministic malformed parser inputs (no crash/panic, not full fuzzing)
fuzzing: No libFuzzer/coverage-guided fuzzing; only reproducible malformed source corpus
historical: GNU Prolog C baseline retained as offline oracle; differential ISO suite not yet run on new runtime

matched_baselines: Analytic expected Horn solutions from fixed examples, independent of engine output
Historical GNU Prolog C implementation available offline, not linked
negative_controls: Unknown predicate returns error, not success
Malformed input and nonfinite literal fail
controls.compute_parity: Same Rust source/test suite on both CI ABIs; no cross-language benchmark attempted
controls.parameter_parity: Identical explicit max_steps and max_solutions across ABIs
controls.sampling_parity: Known-answer and alpha-renamed cases fixed before CI; seeded malformed corpus deterministic
controls.data_access_parity: Same bundled program/query source bytes across ABI test jobs

preregistration.prediction: Rust-only binary builds and returns ordered recursive solutions, finite-term checks, bounded errors, and no C engine link on both ABIs
preregistration.primary_metric: All Rust-native known-answer and structural/negative tests pass on ELF64 and i686; any wrong result blocks
preregistration.uncertainty_method: Deterministic functional cases; no statistical population estimate
preregistration.kill_condition: Wrong answer, variable capture, broken rollback, panic on malformed source, ABI failure, cycle acceptance in finite-term mode or hidden C runtime dependency
preregistration.stop_condition: Do not call the complete GNU Prolog rewrite done; expand Rust semantics natively, not by permanent interoperability adapter
preregistration.promotion_rule: H -> M only for observed bounded native Horn-clause subset, not whole Prolog runtime
